newsitem.title: CHINA: China builds record 1.9 mln T of ships in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China builds record 1.9 mln T of ships in 1996.

text.p: China built 1.9 million tonnes of ships in 1996, a record in annual output, the Xinhua quoted the China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC) as saying.

More than 1.6 million tonnes of vessels were exported last year to countries and regions including Norway, Hong Kong, Iran, Canada, Japan, and Singapore, accounting for 84.7 percent of total output, it said. China began construction of another 330,000 tonnes of ships last year, the corporation said.

The corporation had shipbuilding orders for 146 vessels with a combined capacity of 2.27 million tonnes, including 81 vessels for export totalling 1.32 million tonnes, and 49 ships for domestic customers with a combined 950,000 tonnes, it said.
Last year, the amount of shipbuilding orders received was slightly lower than for 1995, when the figure reached 2.48 million tonnes, it said.

"Considering the overall performance of the world shipbuilding market, the (corporation) still became more competitive in 1996," it quoted Li Junfeng, an engineer in the corporation's Production Bureau, as saying.
The contractual value of the corporation's vessels for export reached a combined $1.45 billion, it said.
